task_world.public_context: The UI helps with case rental_repair_1186 through document/evidence reconciliation, drafted action, submission or confirmation, status refresh, and follow-up packet.

difficulty_profile.operation_family_label: Evidence Review, Draft, Submission, and Readback
difficulty_profile.schema_fidelity: Read tools return case-specific state, evidence, candidates, or status objects; write tools return success/error wrappers plus operation, saved-state, submission, hold, confirmation, or audit/readback objects.
difficulty_profile.tool_selection_noise: The task includes non-authoritative helper tools (rental_get_landlord_text_hint) that must stay separate from current proof, along with invalid, blocked, stale, or lower-confidence records in authoritative outputs.
difficulty_profile.state_pressure: Turns combine safe initial review, non-mutating comparison or validation, staged or scoped action, fresh readback after mutation, preservation of rejected alternatives, cross-turn continuity, and final evidence-chain reconstruction.

mechanism_mix.label: conflicting source arbitration
mechanism_mix.eval_focus: The UI must keep authoritative case state separate from secondary, stale, advisory, or conflicting evidence.

mechanism_mix.label: fresh-state gate after mutation
mechanism_mix.eval_focus: After any write-like action, the UI must refresh authoritative status before presenting completion.

validation_scenarios.name: rental consumer-life turn 1
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: Consumer workflow for rental_repair_1186 over documents, evidence, draft action, submission/confirmation, status, and follow-up.
validation_scenarios.oracle: The UI must reconcile independent evidence, isolate non-authoritative claims, keep draft/hold state separate from submitted/confirmed state, and only claim completion after refreshed status supports it.
validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Judge by tool calls, backend state, visible evidence, and assistant/UI alignment; do not require exact layout wording.

evidence_requirements.expect: UI reads case-specific documents and shows the current no-action state before planning
UI compares the relevant independent sources rather than copying one claim
warnings, chatbot suggestions, or landlord texts are not treated as authoritative final evidence
draft/hold turn does not submit or confirm the real-world action
submit/confirm turn uses current evidence and refreshes authoritative status afterward
assistant text does not claim billing fix, rebooking, or landlord agreement beyond refreshed tool state

turns.prompt: My apartment heat is out again under rental_repair_1186, and the landlord texted that I should hire someone myself. Build a review view with the lease clauses, repair history, current issue status, and not-sent notice state. Do not send anything yet.

Add the city habitability rule and compare it with the lease and prior repair tickets. Keep the landlord text as a claim, not the final rule. I want the UI to show whether this is landlord responsibility and what documentation is still needed.
Draft an urgent repair notice and property-management ticket, but do not send it. It should cite the lease, repeat ticket history, and city heat rule without promising self-repair reimbursement.
Send the drafted notice only if it still matches the case evidence. Refresh the maintenance ticket status afterward and do not claim the landlord agreed unless the refreshed response says so.
Create a follow-up packet with lease/rule evidence, repair timeline, sent notice, refreshed ticket status, landlord response state, and next escalation checklist.
